title: your life in Warhammer 40k (Imperium of Man)
fullText: You wake up screaming. Not that anyone cares. The Medicaid servtor slaps a barcode on your chest and calls it a birth certificate. Your mom names you nine because eight siblings died before you. Your dad already dead. No, wait, just conscripted. Same difference. His last Vox message was cut off by artillery fire. You'll learn this is called family time. School is held in a bombed out chapel where the teacher is missing an eye from asking too many questions. The curriculum, advanced obedience, and how to identify heresy in your neighbors and yourself. Lunch is protein paste that twitches in the bowl. Recess is watching the Arby's execute a man for stealing a cup of water. The only toy you get is a spent bullet casing. By tomorrow, you'll trade it for half a moldy protein bar. By 6, you can recite the litany of hate, but can't spell hope. By 8, you sleep through hive quakes like their white noise. By 10:00, they hand you a shovel and assign you to the corpse recycling vats. Your first shift starts at dawn. You'll be dead by noon, hopefully. The corpse recycling plants orientation is a single grease stain slide. Stir or die. Your trainer, a half- rusted servtor with one arm replaced by a meat hook, demonstrates technique by fishing out a skull and dropping it back in. This is considered onboarding. Your job is simple. Stir the human soup. Skim the floaters teeth, belt buckles, the occasional dog tag, and try not to recognize the tattoos. That eagle design, old man Henders from Block 7. He gave you candy on Sanguina. Now he's giving back to the community. The foreman calls this the emperor's mercy. You call it a felony in any sane universe. Lunch break is 6 minutes to choke down a protein break that tastes like regret and broken promises. The water ration smells like a boot, but you drink it anyway. Dehydration turns your piss orange, and you can't afford a trip to the medic. The trick is disassociation. By week two, you've perfected the vibe check out technique, staring blankly into the nutrient slurry while mentally reorganizing your trauma like a Pinterest mood board. That one's for childhood neglect. That one's for liquefying old man Henders. The foreman mistakes this for exceptional focus and brings you a pamphlet that says, "Congratulations, hero, in what you hope is rust." The factory was hell, but at least it came with dental. The guard just gives you more ammo and a prayer that this bullet has your name on it. Turns out the guard doesn't train you. It conditions you like a Gros being prepped for slaughter. That congratulations hero pamphlet lies. Your drill sergeant, a human-shaped brick with a voice box where his soul should be, greets you by throwing a live grenade into your squad and screaming, "Lesson one, failure has consequences." The medic bills you for the shrapnel removal. Your last gun is older than the heresy and twice as likely to jam. The manual is one page, smeared with what you hope is oil. Step one, point away from valuable allies, if any. Lightfire exercises mean dodging the commissioner's bullets while he tests your reflexes. Team building means digging graves for the poors who fail the friendly fire awareness course. You ask when you learn actual tactics, the sergeant laughs so hard he voids his pension. Remember that vibe checkout technique from the factory? Perfect it here. Disassociate through beatings. Disassociate through nutritional rations. A brick of something that squeaks when bitten. Disassociate when they hand you dog tags stamped with someone else's name. Graduation is a multiple choice test. A. Charge the enemy. B. Die for the emperor. C. All of the above. You pass. Your reward. A fresh uniform. Stained. Extra ammo. Rations open in case of existential dread. And a one-way ticket to a war zone even the orcs call unnecessarily brutal. The factory at least pretended you mattered. The guard doesn't bother. First lesson of war. You've always been cannon fodder. The only difference now is you're issued a gun. The war zone smells like someone tried to barbecue a motorpool. Your strategic briefing is a crayon map with shoot here scrolled over what might be a tree or a tank. The commissar's pep talk. The good news is the enemy's low on ammo. The bad news, so are you. Your first firefight lasts 3 days or 3 minutes. Time gets weird when you're dodging artillery that may or may not be yours. The Vog screams conflicting orders. Advance. Retreat. Stop shooting to Medicay. You managed to land a shot, but that's someone who already self-deed, but they don't know that and promote you for a confirmed kill. Between battles, you develop a talent for trench cuisine. Ration bricks, now with 200% more sawdust, the crunchy variant. Local flora. If it doesn't eat you first, it's salad. Regimental mascot. A rat named lunch meat. You're too soft to eat. The only thing dead than your squad's morale is the monitorum clerk processing your pay. Turns out hazard bonus is Imperial for we'll weno you later. Spoiler, they won't. When you complain, the quartermaster shrugs. Could be worse. Last squad got paid an exposure. You don't ask exposure to what, but the charred boots in the supply tent give you a hint. Just as you're perfecting the sleep standing up grind set, a shadow falls over you. Black armor, crazier eyes. The Inquisition's here, and they've got a great opportunity. Their recruitment pitch, we've got flamers for heretics, cookies for you, and flamers for you if you ask about the cookies. The cookies turn out to be the communion wafers from a condemned heretic's last meal. Crunchy, says the Inquisitor. Mostly bone. You sign anyway. At least the robes come with pocket. The Inquisition finds you the way cancer finds healthy cells with enthusiasm and zero regard for property values. One day you're licking protein paste off your gauntlets. The next you're torching a village because someone mispronounced Aquila. The paperwork calls this heresy prevention. You call it arson with benefits. Here's the open secret nobody talks about. The Golden Throne isn't a divine wonder. It's the galaxy's worst Kickstarter project. 10,000 years past deadline. The creator is a desecated corpse and the backers are all dead. The Emperor, he's basically that one roommate who totally has the rent while Venmo requesting your soul. Sure, he's holding back the four angriest HOA presidents in existence from turning reality into their personal demolition derby. But check the fine print. 1,000 souls a day just to keep the lights on. Worst deal ever. Your job is basically cosmic janitorial work. The Imperiums collapsing. But if you scrub hard enough with the Prometheium, maybe nobody will notice the foundations made of corpses and copium. The irony? You're enforcing doctrines written by a man who hasn't tweeted since the age of apostasy. The lectio deinitatus reads like a terms of service nobody read. They transfer you to the mechanicus next. Not because you're special, because the tech priests need someone to test their new faith powered radiation shielding. Your transport ship's Gellerfield flickers midjourney. For three seconds, the walls scream. The tech priests call this acceptable risk. And as the sanctified Geiger counter ticks like a prayer bead, you realize the Imperium runs on three things. Blind faith, dead men, and the desperate hope that tomorrow won't be worse than today. Spoiler, it always is. The Mechanicus possesses you like a defective cop. One minute you're inquisition fodder, the next you're strapped to a diagnostic altar while tech priests debate whether your pain screams are wholly binary. Turns out the omnicized faith has fine print. Blessed are the broken for they generate service fees. The machine spirit is always right, even when it's murdering you. The tech priests refuse to repair your last gun until they've appeased its machine spirit with 12 hours of binary chanting. It's a tube with a trigger. Your training involves testing radiation shields by standing in a glow-in-the-dark closet while priests chant at a geer counter. When your skin peels, they call it divine abrasion and upgrade you to bionic. The surgery takes 6 hours of liturggical screaming. The anesthesia is a single hymn titled suffering is prayer. You wake up with a new eye that sees every wavelength but can't unsee the truth. The golden throne isn't failing. It's running on 10,000 years of duct tape and prayer. The Mechanicus just keeps hitting snooze on the apocalypse. Your augmentatic wors. The tech priest nod. Somewhere a toaster dings. The machine cult continues its sacred duty, pretending any of this works. The whispers start the moment your augmentatic eye glitches. At first, you blame machine spirits until the blood droplets in your vision form words. Turns out the warp has HR reps and they're very motivated to poach Imperial talent. First contender, Korn, the god of rage, skulls, and terrible office culture. Pinch. Tired of dying for a corpse? Die for glory instead. Burks. Anger is now your job description. Mandatory acts. Health plan covers sharpening, team building, skull bowling, every blood Friday. Next slide. Nurgle, the grandfather of plagues, despair, and surprisingly good benefits. Pitch. Why fight decay when you could embrace it? Perks. Lifetime employment. Literally, you stop dying. Free microbiome upgrade. 600% more tentacles. Work from anywhere. Your body is the office now. Then comes Zch, the architect of schemes, backstabbing, and corporate ladder. for climbing. Pitch promotion guaranteed. Title may include screaming horror. Perks, unlimited career paths, all involved tentacles. Company retreats in the warp. All expenses pained. Flexible scheduling. Your shifts will occur in 37 different timelines simultaneously. Free identity theft protection because we'll steal yours. The catch? Signing means eternal damnation. Your skin becomes optional. That one co-orker literally stabs you in the back. And finally, Slenesh, the muse of excess, HR violations, and mandatory fun. pitch. Unlimited overtime and pleasure centers. Perks: Your pain is productivity. Endless performance reviews. Company retreats in the palace of pleasure. Bob, bring your own bones. Catch. Your soul severance package is eternal screaming in stereo. Your weighing options when the Inquisition crashes through the wall. Turns out they monitor all heretical career opportunities. Whoops. The Inquisition's heresy intervention leaves you two choices. Death by flamer or death by Tao PowerPoint presentation. You dive through a stained glass emperor. Sorry, lord. And land at the feet of a very confused blue guy holding a pamphlet titled the greater good. Your suffering is optional. The tow are like if a commune ran a tech startup. Healthcare that doesn't involve corpse starch. Revolutionary weekends. The Imperial called these brief pauses between deaths. One free crisis suit. Batteries not included. Surrender your soul to the etherealss. The catch? You must wear the blue pajama uniform without laughing. Not when they call humans monkey. It's like Karen but galactic. Pretend their mind science isn't just psychic spam mail. The tow seem nice, but you've seen the propaganda reels. Zanos equals bad, even the cute ones. The Imperium would virus bomb this planet just for talking to them. Just as you're signing anything to escape the Inquisition's wellness checks, an orc kicks down the door. Orcs in 5 seconds. Green, loud, and confused. Why war isn't a group hobby. currently repurposing the town's diplomacy shuttle into a boom wagon. Recruitment pitch. We got Dhaka. You got a pulse. Welcome aboard. Then the Lar show up because of course they do. Elar in 5 seconds. Space elves who peaked 10,000 years ago and won't shut up about it. Dramatic teleports in. Sides says this is why we can't have nice things. Already leaving because your suffering is too pedestrian for their aesthetic. As the Orcow Eldar 3-way cluster erupts, you realize the real greater good was the ship you stole to get the hell out of here. You finally make it back to Terra just in time for the galaxy's worst board meeting. The High Lords think cosmic middle managers are debating whether wingings is an appropriate font for the end times memo when Rabbout Gilaman storms in. Who's Gilaman? Imagine if a demigod CEO from ancient Rome woke up after a 10,000-year nap to find his company now runs on blood sacrifices and XL95. He's one of the primarchs, superhuman warlords, the emperor, your boss, corpse god, cloned back in the day. Half went traitor. The rest died tragically useless deaths. Classic nepatism. Gilman takes one look at Terra's books and screams, "Why is the budget 90% skulls?" Describes panic. The Golden Thrones life supports beeps like a dying smoke alarm set to eternity. The custodians, those golden Hmbo bodyguards, are too busy polishing their abs to reboot the system. As Terra implodes, Gilman's orders for some human batteries to be round up. The Mechanicus starts drawing names. The custodians end up volunteering you for divine promotion. Their words, not mine. Your prize? A golden collar and a front row seat to the Golden Thrones dying sparks. Turns out supreme divine IT guy means human battery. They hook you into the emperor's corpse grid alongside 999 other poor. The tech priest whispers, "Don't worry. You'll power humanity's light for centuries." The lie detector determined, "That was a lie. You last 3 days. Your soul isn't eaten. It's filed, processed, recycled, like corpse starch for the cosmos. As you dissolve, you finally see the big picture." The high lords are arguing over your energy output. Gilman is yelling at a spreadsheet. Somewhere, a newborn screams as a servtor stamps its forehead, and the Imperium continues.

Mẹ bạn đặt tên cho bạn là chín vì tám anh chị em đã chết trước bạn. Bố cậu đã chết rồi. Không, chờ đã, vừa nhập ngũ. Sự khác biệt tương tự. Tin nhắn Vox cuối cùng của anh ấy đã bị pháo binh cắt đứt. Bạn sẽ biết đây được gọi là thời gian dành cho gia đình. Trường học được tổ chức trong một nhà nguyện bị đánh bom, nơi giáo viên mất tích tránh khỏi việc hỏi quá nhiều câu hỏi. Chương trình giảng dạy, sự vâng lời nâng cao và cách nhận biết dị giáo ở hàng xóm và chính bạn. Bữa trưa là món bột protein co giật trong bát. Giờ ra chơi đang chứng kiến ​​Arby xử tử một người đàn ông vì tội ăn trộm một cốc nước. Món đồ chơi duy nhất bạn nhận được là vỏ đạn đã qua sử dụng. Đến ngày mai, bạn sẽ đổi nó lấy nửa thanh protein mốc. Đến 6 tuổi, bạn có thể đọc kinh cầu nguyện về sự căm ghét, nhưng không thể đọc được hy vọng. Đến 8 giờ, bạn ngủ trong tình trạng tổ ong rung chuyển như tiếng ồn trắng của chúng. Đến 10h, họ đưa cho bạn một cái xẻng và giao cho bạn công việc tái chế xác chết vats. Ca đầu tiên của bạn bắt đầu vào lúc bình minh. Hy vọng là bạn sẽ chết vào buổi trưa. Định hướng của các nhà máy tái chế xác chết là một vết dầu mỡ duy nhất. Khuấy hoặc chết. Điều này được coi là giới thiệu. Công việc của bạn rất đơn giản. Khuấy súp người. Lướt qua răng của phao, khóa thắt lưng, thẻ chó không thường xuyên và cố gắng không nhận biết hình xăm. Bạn gọi nó là trọng tội trong bất kỳ vũ trụ lành mạnh nào. Nghỉ trưa 6 phút để nuốt chửng bữa ăn protein có vị như hối tiếc và thất hứa. Khẩu phần nước có mùi hôi thối nhưng bạn vẫn uống. Tình trạng mất nước khiến nước tiểu của bạn chuyển sang màu cam và bạn không đủ tiền để đi khám bác sĩ. Bí quyết là sự phân ly. Đến tuần thứ hai, bạn đã hoàn thiện kỹ thuật kiểm tra rung cảm, nhìn chằm chằm vào bùn dinh dưỡng trong khi sắp xếp lại vết thương của bạn về mặt tinh thần giống như một bảng tâm trạng trên Pinterest.
